classification.difficultyReason: Model different running distances and finishing times with two variables, eliminate one variable and reject an infeasible quadratic root.

content.prompt: Two boys, one of whom can run $1\text{ m/s}$ faster than the other, compete in a $400\text{ m}$ race. The slower competitor is given a $20\text{ m}$ start and loses by $10$ seconds. What was the average speed of each runner (correct to three decimal places)?

answer.short:
Slower runner: $4.844\text{ m/s}$; faster runner: $5.844\text{ m/s}$.

Use distance = speed × time for each runner and eliminate the time variable.
answer.worked:
Let the slower runner's speed be $v\text{ m/s}$ and the faster runner's time be $t$ seconds. The slower runner covers $380\text{ m}$ in $(t+10)$ seconds; the faster runner covers $400\text{ m}$ at $(v+1)\text{ m/s}$.

$$\begin{align*}v(t+10)&=380\\(v+1)t&=400\\t&=\frac{400}{v+1}\end{align*}$$

Substitute for $t$:

$$\begin{align*}v\left(\frac{400}{v+1}+10\right)&=380\\400v+10v(v+1)&=380(v+1)\\10v^2+30v-380&=0\\v^2+3v-38&=0\\v&=\frac{-3\pm\sqrt{161}}{2}\end{align*}$$

The negative root is impossible for a speed. Therefore the slower runner's speed is $\dfrac{\sqrt{161}-3}{2}\approx4.844\text{ m/s}$, and the faster runner's speed is $\dfrac{\sqrt{161}-1}{2}\approx5.844\text{ m/s}$, both correct to three decimal places.

Check using the exact speeds:

$$\frac{380}{(\sqrt{161}-3)/2}-\frac{400}{(\sqrt{161}-1)/2}=10\text{ s}.$$
